research_mode: official Home Office 2026 technical annex only; outcomes-framework history, purposes and alternative-offence outcomes; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Pre-April-2013 detections regime
verified_claims: official statistics before April 2013 focused on detections
detections included charge and caution resolutions
the later outcomes framework is a broader regime
limitations: detection-era categories are not directly interchangeable with current outcome categories
historical regime labels are not parcel-safety indicators

sources.name: Broader outcomes supply from April 2014
verified_claims: police forces supplied the broader set of outcomes from April 2014
first provisional statistics under the framework appeared in the year-ending March 2014 bulletin
Home Office statisticians developed the series with forces and users
limitations: provisional and mature framework editions require version context
April 2014 is a supply-framework boundary rather than an incident-date boundary

sources.name: No outcome favoured by framework
verified_claims: the framework aimed to recognise the full range of disposals
no single outcome should be favoured over another
appropriateness rather than target hitting is the stated emphasis
limitations: outcome numbers must not be ranked as a quality ladder
different disposals reflect case context and professional judgement

sources.name: Victim-oriented framework purpose
verified_claims: the framework was intended to support a victim-oriented approach
it sought to remove perverse incentives from locally set detection targets
officers were encouraged to consider victims' needs and engagement
limitations: stated policy purpose is not direct evidence of individual victim experience
outcome mix alone cannot measure service quality

sources.name: Transparency and accountability purpose
verified_claims: the broader information was intended to give a richer picture of crime handling
the public can use it for accountability and constructive engagement
assigning an outcome helps explain police activity
limitations: transparency data do not establish causal effectiveness
area-level accountability information is not parcel-level risk evidence

sources.name: Recorded and charged offence distinction
verified_claims: a suspect may be charged or cautioned for a different offence from the recorded offence
CPS charging standards can direct an alternative offence
the recorded offence can remain legally correct while the disposal uses another offence
limitations: alternative-offence outcomes are not recording errors by default
charged-offence labels must not overwrite the original recorded-offence field

sources.name: Outcome 1A alternative charge or summons
verified_claims: outcome 1A records a charge or summons relating to an alternative offence
it follows CPS charging standards and Home Office recording rules
subsequent acquittal does not change the outcome definition
limitations: outcome 1A must remain distinct from outcome 1
it does not imply conviction or offence equivalence

sources.name: Outcome 2A alternative youth caution
verified_claims: outcome 2A records a youth caution for an alternative offence
the alternative follows charging standards and recording rules
it is separate from the standard youth-caution outcome
limitations: outcome 2A must not be merged into outcome 2 without an explicit grouping rule
the outcome does not expose personal identity

sources.name: Outcome 3A alternative adult caution
verified_claims: outcome 3A records an adult caution for an alternative offence
the alternative follows CPS standards and Home Office rules
it is separate from the standard adult-caution outcome
limitations: outcome 3A requires edition-aware coding
it must not be treated as a severity rank

sources.name: Alternative-outcome implementation dates
verified_claims: outcomes 1A 2A and 3A were introduced voluntarily in April 2016
they became mandatory in April 2017
their purpose is to preserve the difference between recorded and disposed offence
limitations: pre-mandatory and mandatory periods require implementation metadata
absence before adoption must not be interpreted as no alternative-offence disposals
